# Native iOS

The iOS project — including the Widget extension target — lives in `ios/`. The `apple/` folder at the repo root holds APNs push certificates only; do not put native code there.

## Workspace, Not Project

**Always open `ios/Aura.xcworkspace`** — never `ios/Aura.xcodeproj`. The workspace is checked into the repo and is also (re)generated by CocoaPods on `pod install`. Opening the bare `.xcodeproj` will not link any pod dependencies.

## Schemes

- `Aura` — main app
- `Aura WidgetExtension` — iOS Widget

Both schemes are checked in under `ios/Aura.xcodeproj/xcshareddata/xcschemes/`.

## Pod Install

```bash
cd ios && pod install --repo-update && cd ..
```

CocoaPods is pinned in the `Gemfile`: run `bundle install`, then call it as `bundle exec pod`.

After **any** change to `package.json` that adds or upgrades a native module, run `pod install` again.

## Common Failures + Recovery

- **"No bundle URL present" on launch** → Metro isn't running. `npm run start` first.
- **Pods out of sync after pull** → `cd ios && bundle exec pod install --repo-update && cd ..`.
- **Build cache weirdness** → `npm run setup` (full clean reinstall, including pods).
- **Widget extension fails to build** → check the `Aura WidgetExtension` scheme is checked in and that the App Group entitlement matches.
- **`Build input file cannot be found: src/cask/GoogleService-Info.plist`** → the cask isn't seeded. `src/cask/` is gitignored, so a new worktree or clone has no config at all. `bash scripts/sync-cask.sh seed --apply` then `bash scripts/sync-cask.sh switch dev`.
- **`error: Node.js not found` / `Command PhaseScriptExecution failed with a nonzero exit code`** → the JS bundle phase found no Node. Run `nvm use && npm install --legacy-peer-deps`; its postinstall writes `ios/.xcode.env.local` with that Node. **Don't hand-write that file** — see [`.xcode.env` / `.xcode.env.local`](#xcodeenv--xcodeenvlocal--how-xcode-finds-node) for why, and for how the phase resolves Node.
- **`rbenv: pod: command not found`** → run `bundle install`. CocoaPods is pinned in the `Gemfile`, and `.ruby-version` is `3.3.11`, so it has to be installed into that Ruby. **Ignore the follow-up hint** — rbenv helpfully lists the Ruby versions where `pod` *does* exist (`The 'pod' command exists in these Ruby versions: 3.2.0, 3.3.0`), which reads like "switch Ruby" and is the wrong fix. After `bundle install`, invoke it as `bundle exec pod`, not bare `pod`.
- **`'RCTBridgeModule.h' file not found (in target 'react-native-mixpanel' …)`**, or any other "header not found" in a library `patches/` covers → a patch never applied. **After a React Native upgrade, reinstall with `npm ci --legacy-peer-deps`, not `npm install`.** `npm install` leaves a package in place when its version is unchanged, so a copy patched against the *old* React Native keeps that state, the new patch no longer applies to it, and `patch-package` reports `finished with 2 error(s)` in the middle of the install log — while `npm install` itself still exits 0. The build then fails a long way from the cause. Verified after the 0.87.1 upgrade: over a 0.77 tree, `react-native-mixpanel` and `react-native-image-crop-picker` failed to patch; `npm ci` (which wipes `node_modules`) applied all 30. Follow it with `bundle exec pod install` — and if that stops on `hermes-engine` with *"differs from the version stored in `Pods/Local Podspecs`"*, delete `ios/Pods/Local Podspecs` (generated, gitignored) and re-run rather than `pod update hermes-engine`, which rewrites `Podfile.lock` away from master's. (ENG-1462.)
- **`fatal error: module 'RCTDeprecation' in precompiled file …`** → **not a failure.** Clang emits it on every archive of this project and recovers; the module is rebuilt and the build continues. Deleting `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/ModuleCache.noindex` does not stop it — it regenerates within the same build. It is usually the last `❌` before the real error, which is why it misleads. Find the real cause under `The following build commands failed:`, not in the last `❌` line.
- **`error: exportArchive Cloud signing permission error`** / **`Provisioning profile "…" doesn't include signing certificate "…"`** → the archive succeeded and the *export* failed: no installed provisioning profile contains the distribution cert in this keychain, and an App Store Connect API key cannot mint cloud-managed signing assets at any role. Import a `.p12` for a cert the profiles already contain, or archive+export once from Xcode.app signed into an Apple ID with Admin on team `9C8CA87JCB` to regenerate the profiles around your cert. Creating another certificate is not a fix. The `release-ios` skill's pre-flight now catches this in about a second rather than ten minutes in.

## Building from CLI

```bash
# Smoke build (no signing) — useful from CI / agents
xcodebuild -workspace ios/Aura.xcworkspace -scheme Aura \
  -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' \
  build -quiet -allowProvisioningUpdates

# Archive (release)
npm run archive
```

**Don't add `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` if you intend to launch the result.** It's
tempting on an unsigned host, and it does make the compile succeed — but it also
skips framework embedding, so the app builds and then dies at launch:

```
Library not loaded: @rpath/aosl.framework/aosl   (Agora)
```

The flag is fine for answering "does it compile" and useless for anything else.
When you need a **runnable** app on a simulator, use
`bash AuraSimTests/Scripts/sim_install.sh`, which builds and installs a
release-config `Aura.app` with frameworks embedded.

## Releasing

**Use the [`release-ios` skill](../skills/release-ios/SKILL.md)** — it is the
entry point for a release:

```bash
python3 .claude/skills/release-ios/scripts/release_ios.py plan --env prod --level patch
```

It bumps the version, calls the fastlane lane below to archive and upload, then
lands the bump on `master` through a PR, tags the squash-merge commit, and
publishes that tag as a GitHub release. The lanes below are what it drives; run
them by hand only to build without releasing.

### The lanes

Lanes live in `ios/fastlane/Fastfile` and are run from `ios/`.

```bash
cd ios && bundle exec fastlane ios release_prod
```

The release lane builds and ships. It runs four steps and **does not touch git
history** — no version bump, no tag:

1. **Version and build** — read from the project (set beforehand via `set_version`)
2. **Apply cask env** — `scripts/sync-cask.sh switch <env>` (repoint the symlinks
   at `src/cask/<env>/`), then clear DerivedData
3. **Build and archive** — Release config, local automatic signing
   - **3b. Size guard** — measure the `.ipa`, refuse to upload one over budget
     (see [Size guard](#size-guard))
4. **Upload** — TestFlight, then Bugsnag dSYMs + JS source map

| Lane | What it does |
|------|--------------|
| `release_prod` / `release_dev` | The four-step build + upload |
| `set_version` | Step 1's input — `version:X.Y.Z build:N`, writes all three configs |
| `cask_prod` / `cask_dev` | Step 2 alone — point cask at that env + clean caches, no build |
| `version` | Print the version/build/tag that would be released (no side effects) |
| `ci_release_prod` / `ci_release_dev` | CircleCI entry points — see [Release via CircleCI](#release-via-circleci). Currently unused; don't run by hand. |

`skip_testflight:true` archives without uploading. It does **not** avoid needing
an App Store Connect key: xcodebuild uses it for `-allowProvisioningUpdates`.

Two guards run before the archive, both skipped on CI (where a checkout is dirty
after `npm`/`pod install` and the tag exists by definition): the working tree must
be clean, and the release tag must not already exist. There is no branch check —
the skill builds from the release branch on purpose, so a failed archive never
leaves a bump merged to `master`.

### Why tagging is not in the lane

The tag has to point at the commit that lands on `master`. `master` is protected
so a bump commit can't be pushed from a build lane, and because merges are
squashed, a tag on the local bump commit would point at a commit that never
lands. So the skill merges the bump PR and tags the resulting commit — after
asserting its tree matches the one that was archived.

This also means `version:` / `build:` are **refused** by the release lanes. Bump
via `set_version`, which the skill calls.

### The cask layout

Both envs are cached locally and the three build-critical paths are symlinks into
the active one, so switching envs is a symlink flip:

```
src/cask/{dev,prod}/{GoogleService-Info.<env>.plist, google-services.<env>.json, meals.<env>.js}
src/cask/GoogleService-Info.plist  -> prod/GoogleService-Info.prod.plist   # e.g.
src/cask/meals.js                 -> prod/meals.prod.js
```

Android reaches its own config the same way, through a link `switch` maintains at
`android/app/google-services.json` — see [native-android.md](native-android.md).
A cache missing that file does **not** abort an iOS release, since an archive
never reads it.

`src/cask/<env>/` is the source of truth for a build, kept current by hand — the
release lane never reaches out to a drive or a network for it. Full detail:
[.claude/skills/sync-cask/SKILL.md](../skills/sync-cask/SKILL.md).

Step 2 **aborts the release** if `meals.<env>.js` doesn't carry every key
`src/cask/meals.sample.js` declares, filled in. A hand-maintained cask drifts —
a key added to one env's file and not the other's builds fine and ships a feature
that silently does nothing, which is why this is checked before the archive and
not after. If it fires, the fix is in `src/cask/<env>/`, not in the lane.

**Version and build land in a PR, never in the release lane** — the `release-ios`
skill automates exactly that, so the whole flow is one command:

```bash
python3 .claude/skills/release-ios/scripts/release_ios.py run --env prod --level patch
```

It branches off `origin/master`, calls `set_version`, commits, archives and
uploads, and only then opens the PR — so a failed archive costs a local branch
and nothing more. After the squash merge it tags that commit, having first
confirmed the merged tree is identical to the one it archived, then publishes the
tag as a GitHub release (`--no-github-release` opts out). Release tags sit
on ordinary `master` commits (`3.19.140-1` → `c43728ba8`, a regular
squash-merge), which is what that ordering preserves.

By hand, the same shape is:

```bash
cd ios && bundle exec fastlane ios set_version version:3.19.142 build:1   # in a branch
cd ios && bundle exec fastlane ios release_prod                            # build + upload
# open a PR, merge it, tag the squash-merge commit, then `gh release create` that tag
```

Note `CFBundleVersion` in `ios/Aura/Info.plist` reads `$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)`
as of this change. It was previously hardcoded to `1`, so build numbers never
reached the binary — which is likely why almost every historical tag ends in `-1`
and the patch version was bumped instead.

Version reads and writes go through the `xcodeproj` gem, not text parsing of
`project.pbxproj`. The file has three configurations (Debug/Release/**Staging**)
and quotes identifiers containing `-`, both of which line-oriented parsing gets
wrong. Writes are surgical — only the version lines change.

### Font licensing gate

**The release lane enforces this — you do not have to remember it.** `deploy` calls
`verify_production_fonts!` before it touches credentials or starts the archive, so a
build carrying trial-licensed fonts fails in seconds instead of shipping.

To check by hand at any point:

```bash
npm run fonts:check
```

Exits non-zero and names every offender if a **trial-licensed** font is registered in
`assets/fonts/`, the Android assets folder, `Info.plist`'s `UIAppFonts`, or the Xcode
project. The redesign's Season faces shipped as `-TRIAL` evaluation builds until Charter
and Nunito replaced them, and ABC Otto did until the licensed Light, Light Italic and
Regular cuts replaced it (Nov 2026). No trial face is bundled now. A trial face is **not licensed for
distribution** — fine on a feature branch and for internal builds, a licensing violation in
a store release.

Deliberately **not** in PR CI: the redesign stack has to keep merging against the trial
faces while the licensed ones are procured, so `master` carries them for a while. That
makes the release lane the last point in the pipeline that can stop them reaching users,
which is why the check lives there rather than in a runbook step someone has to remember.

`fastlane ios release_prod allow_trial_fonts:true` overrides it. That exists so a release
is never hard-blocked by a licensing question someone has already answered — it has to be
typed deliberately and prints a warning into the build log, so it cannot happen by
accident or pass unnoticed afterwards.

When the licensed faces land they drop the `-TRIAL` suffix from both filename and
PostScript name, so the check starts passing on its own; the `fontFamily` values in
`src/styles/redesign/fonts.js` need the same rename in the same change.

### Size guard

**The release lane enforces this too.** After the archive and before the upload,
`deploy` runs `scripts/measure-ios-app-size.sh` on the `.ipa` gym produced. The script
prints the bundle by bucket (frameworks by vendor, main binary, JS bundle, RN assets,
bundled audio, fonts) so every release log carries a breakdown, then applies two lines:

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `IPA_WARN_MB` | 177 | Over this, the processed download will exceed Apple's 200 MB cellular limit. Warns. |
| `IPA_BUDGET_MB` | 190 | Over this, the lane refuses to upload. Fails. |

The numbers are anchored on Apple's email for 3.21.1 (PROD-5530): 180.4 MB submitted
became 203.7 MB once processed, so 200 MB processed is about 177 MB submitted. Both the
script and these constants use **decimal megabytes** (1 MB = 1,000,000 bytes), the unit App
Store Connect reports in — not MiB, which would read ~5% smaller and let a build past. The
budget is a **regression ceiling**, not the target — ratchet it down as each size PR lands
and re-measures. Never raise it to make a release pass.

The guard sits between archive and upload on purpose. It is the only point where the
artifact exists and nothing has shipped yet; a check that fails *after* the upload would
strand a build on TestFlight that the `release-ios` skill treats as unshipped.

`fastlane ios release_prod size_budget_mb:195` overrides the budget for one run — for a
release that must go out over a known, accepted regression. Like `allow_trial_fonts`, it
has to be typed deliberately and prints a warning into the build log.

To measure any build by hand — an `.ipa`, an `.xcarchive`, or a bare `.app` — without
Xcode:

```bash
bash scripts/measure-ios-app-size.sh DerivedData-CLI/Build/Products/Release-iphonesimulator/Aura.app
```

Simulator builds carry both `x86_64` and `arm64` slices, so their code buckets read roughly
double a device build. Compare like with like.

### One-time setup

1. `bundle install` at the repo root (fastlane and the Bugsnag plugin are in the root `Gemfile`; plugins are declared in `ios/fastlane/Pluginfile`).
2. Copy `ios/fastlane/.env.sample` → `ios/fastlane/.env` and fill in the App Store Connect API key values.

**Auth is an App Store Connect API key, not an Apple ID.** Same approach as
AuraConsumerApp. A `.p8` team key doesn't break when someone leaves and doesn't
trip 2FA on a non-interactive host; the lane clears any stale `FASTLANE_USER` /
`FASTLANE_PASSWORD` from the environment so they can't silently take precedence.
`ios/fastlane/.env` and `**/fastlane/*.p8` are gitignored — never commit either.
`ios/fastlane/.env` is fastlane's own env file and is unrelated to the JS bundle;
the repo-root `.env` no longer exists (PROD-4975).

Signing is local + automatic: the distribution cert must already be in the
release host's keychain. There is no `match` / certs repo.

## Release via CircleCI — currently DISABLED

The same lanes can also run on CircleCI (ENGMOB-818), but the `ios_testflight`
job is **commented out of the workflow** in `.circleci/config.yml`. Two
independent reasons:

1. **None of its six environment variables are set on the project.** The job's own
   pre-flight step fails on the first one it can't find, so every release-tag push
   produced a red build that shipped nothing.
2. **It would double-build.** The `release-ios` skill archives and uploads from the
   release host *before* opening the bump PR, then tags the merge commit. A
   tag-triggered CI job would archive and upload a second binary under the same
   version+build, and App Store Connect rejects that.

`.circleci/config.yml` currently runs one job:

| Job | Runs on | When |
|-----|---------|------|
| `test` | Docker (`cimg/node`) | every commit and tag — lint only |
| ~~`ios_testflight`~~ | macOS (`m4pro.medium`, Xcode 26.2.0) | **disabled** — job kept, workflow entry commented out |

**To re-enable:** set the six variables (see `ios/fastlane/.env.sample`), restore
the workflow entry, **and** switch the skill off local builds — otherwise (2)
bites on the first release. The two cannot both run.

The lane cross-checks `CIRCLE_TAG` against the version in `project.pbxproj` and
aborts on a mismatch, so a tag pushed before the bump PR merges fails the job in
seconds rather than uploading a binary whose `CFBundleVersion` disagrees with its
tag. That check is dormant while CI is off (`CIRCLE_TAG` is never set) and stays
correct if it comes back.

The workflow ran **`ci_release_prod` only**. `ci_release_dev` exists and works,
but wiring it up needs a second set of `*_DEV_BASE64` cask variables and a second
workflow entry.

`ci_release_prod` / `ci_release_dev` are the same `deploy` code path as
`release_prod` / `release_dev`, with one flag:

- **`skip_cask`** — `src/cask/` is gitignored, so a CI checkout has no env caches
  for `scripts/sync-cask.sh` to switch to. The job restores
  `src/cask/` from environment variables and the lane calls `verify_cask!`
  instead of copying. That still asserts `meals.js` declares the env being
  released, so a mis-set variable fails the job rather than shipping dev Firebase
  config to TestFlight.
There is no `skip_tag` flag any more — the lane never tags, on CI or locally.
The guards that used to hang off it (clean tree, tag-does-not-exist) are now
skipped via `ci?`, since a CI checkout is dirty after `npm`/`pod install` and the
tag is the trigger rather than an output.

### CI signing

A fresh macOS executor has an empty keychain, so `setup_ci_signing!` imports the
distribution certificate from `IOS_DIST_CERT_P12_BASE64` into a throwaway
keychain that dies with the executor. Still our own certificate — carried in
rather than pre-installed. Swapping to a team-owned key issued to a system user,
or to `match`, replaces that one method and nothing else.

Automatic signing means **xcodebuild**, not fastlane, fetches the provisioning
profiles for the three bundle IDs the archive embeds — `com.AuraMobile`,
`com.AuraMobile.Aura-Widget`, `com.AuraMobile.OneSignalNotificationServiceExtension`.
(The `AuraWatch` targets are still in the project but dead: not in the `Aura`
scheme, and the Embed Watch Content phase is empty. `ios/AuraWatch/Info.plist`
doesn't even exist. So they need no profile — and nothing builds them.)
Interactively xcodebuild uses the signed-in Xcode account; on CI it needs the
API key passed explicitly, which is what `xcode_asc_auth_args` adds
(`-authenticationKeyPath` / `-authenticationKeyID` / `-authenticationKeyIssuerID`).
Without those, the archive fails with `No profiles for 'com.AuraMobile' were
found` — which reads like a portal problem and isn't.

### Environment variables

Set under CircleCI → Project Settings → Environment Variables. The job checks all
of them up front and names the missing one, so it fails in seconds rather than
after ~15 minutes of `npm install` + `pod install`. Full descriptions and the
`base64` command for each are in `ios/fastlane/.env.sample`.

`APP_STORE_CONNECT_API_KEY_BASE64`, `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID`,
`APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID`, `IOS_DIST_CERT_P12_BASE64`,
`IOS_DIST_CERT_PASSWORD`, `MEALS_JS_PROD_BASE64`,
`GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_PROD_BASE64`.

### Notes

- **macOS credits are a prerequisite.** The deploy job needs a CircleCI plan with
  macOS minutes; the Docker `test` job is unaffected either way.
- **The job's `nvm alias default` is what decides Xcode's Node.** `.xcode.env.local`
  is gitignored, so a fresh CI checkout starts without it — the job's "Select Node
  from .nvmrc" step puts the right node on `PATH`, and every later step inherits
  it, including the shell Xcode runs the "Bundle React Native code and images"
  phase in. `npm install` then writes `.xcode.env.local` from that same node
  (postinstall), so from that point the path is pinned rather than
  PATH-resolved — same version either way, because the alias step ran first. If
  the phase ever reports `Error: Node.js not found`, the alias step is where to
  look. See the section below for the full resolution order.
- **Android is not wired up.** There is no Play Store service-account key in CI
  and `android/app/build.gradle` still carries its keystore passwords inline — a
  separate piece of work, not a line to add to this job.
- The Xcode image is pinned deliberately. It's the compiler and SDK a shipped
  binary is built against, so keep `xcode:` aligned with the Xcode the release
  host uses for `release_prod` and bump both together.

## `.xcode.env` / `.xcode.env.local` — how Xcode finds Node

Xcode runs a build phase in a **non-login shell**, so `nvm` / `fnm` / `asdf` never
load and `command -v node` frequently finds nothing. These two files are React
Native's answer. `with-environment.sh` sources `ios/.xcode.env`, then
`ios/.xcode.env.local`, and the "Bundle React Native code and images" phase builds
the JS bundle with the `NODE_BINARY` that comes out.

**You should never have to touch either file.** Two mechanisms resolve Node, in
the order the phase applies them — later wins:

| # | Mechanism | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ios/.xcode.env` → `command -v node` | a machine whose node is on the default `PATH` (Homebrew, system) |
| 2 | `ios/.xcode.env.local` → absolute `NODE_BINARY`, written by **every `npm install`** | everything else, and it is what normally decides |

Mechanism 2 is `scripts/write-xcode-env-local.js`, chained off `postinstall`
(`npx jetify && node scripts/write-xcode-env-local.js`). It records
`process.execPath` — the exact interpreter that ran the install.

**If that Node isn't the `.nvmrc` one, the install fails.** The pin is whatever
ran the install, so installing under the wrong Node would aim Xcode at the wrong
Node — a non-zero `postinstall` refuses that outright rather than warning about
it. Two consequences worth knowing: no pin is written (nothing wrong is left
behind), and `prepare` never runs, so `patch-package` hasn't patched the tree. Both
are fixed by the same thing:

```bash
nvm use && npm install --legacy-peer-deps
```

In CI the same gate asserts the runner's Node equals `.nvmrc` — the CircleCI
`cimg/node` tag is the one Node version in the repo written out by hand, and this
is what stops it drifting silently.

Only if both come up empty does the build phase prepend `/opt/homebrew/bin` to
`PATH` as a last resort, then fail with instructions. That prepend used to run
unconditionally, which quietly let Homebrew's node — whatever version it happened
to be — bundle the JS ahead of anything `.nvmrc` said.

**So the fix for any Node-related bundle-phase failure is that same
`nvm use && npm install --legacy-peer-deps`** — mechanism 2 is the one that
normally decides, and an install is what (re)writes it.

There is deliberately **no `.nvmrc` fallback inside `.xcode.env`**. It was tried
and removed, for two reasons worth not rediscovering:

- **It cannot fire when you'd want it to.** `.xcode.env` is sourced only by
  `node_modules/react-native/scripts/xcode/with-environment.sh`, so on a checkout
  with no install the phase never reads it at all. And a build without
  `npm install` is impossible anyway — the phase ends by running
  `react-native-xcode.sh` out of that same `node_modules`. Failing with the
  message above is the correct outcome there, not a gap.
- **Where it could fire, React Native already does it.** With `node_modules`
  present but the pin deleted and no node on `PATH`, `with-environment.sh` falls
  through to its own `find-node-for-xcode.sh`, which reads `.nvmrc` and resolves
  it via nvm — verified. That path is deprecated and prints a warning, so don't
  rely on it; the point is only that a hand-written duplicate bought nothing.

### Why not hardcode a version, and who writes what

Nothing hardcodes a version: `.nvmrc` is the only place one is written, and the
postinstall gate is what holds every other consumer to it. Two files claiming to
be the source of truth is how they drift.

`.xcode.env` stays exactly as React Native generates it, which also means it
**cannot meaningfully be deleted**: `Podfile`'s `prepare_react_native_project!`
calls `ReactNativePodsUtils.create_xcode_env_if_missing`, so a deletion comes
back byte-identical on the next `pod install` as a spurious diff. Note
`create_xcode_env_if_missing` writes `.xcode.env.local` too, but only when it is
absent — so after an `npm install` it is a no-op. (Delete the pin and run only
`pod install`, though, and RN writes it from whatever Node ran *that*, which the
postinstall gate never sees. Re-run `npm install` if you ever hand-delete it.)

| File | Written by | Tracked? |
|---|---|---|
| `ios/.xcode.env` | committed by hand; recreated by `pod install` only if deleted | yes |
| `ios/.xcode.env.local` | `npm install` postinstall, every time | **no**, gitignored — never commit it |

### The failure this replaced

`.xcode.env.local` bakes in an **absolute** path, and the bundle phase's
fallbacks only fire `if [ -z "$NODE_BINARY" ]` — so that value wins over
`nvm use`, over `PATH`, and over anything the release skill sets, silently.

This repo's release checkout was found carrying a hand-written `.xcode.env.local`
from May 2025 pinning `v18.15.0` — an EOL Node, two majors below the `.nvmrc`
pin — so every archive since had bundled its JS with it and nothing reported it.
Nothing rewrote the file, so nothing corrected it. Now every `npm install` does,
which is the whole point of mechanism 2: a pin that cannot go stale, because the
only way to write a wrong one is an install the gate refuses.

The `release-ios` skill still checks the resolved `NODE_BINARY` before the archive
*and* again after `npm ci` + `pod install`, and **refuses to build** when the
bundle phase would not use the `.nvmrc` Node. That check is now a backstop rather
than the only line of defence — an install under the wrong Node no longer gets far
enough to produce a mismatched pin.

## Don't Touch Without Reason

- `ios/Aura.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` — generated/maintained alongside Pod installs and native module additions. Spurious diffs here usually mean someone ran `pod install` with a different RN-CLI version. Coordinate before committing changes here.
- Manual changes to scheme XML (`*.xcscheme`) — Xcode rewrites them; if you must edit, do it through the Manage Schemes UI so the format stays canonical.

## Native Module Linking

React Native uses autolinking for most pods. If you add a native module and it isn't autolinked, check `react-native.config.js` and the module's own podspec. Avoid manual `Podfile` edits when autolinking can do it.

## Bridging to JS

Bridging code lives under `ios/Aura/`. Don't add new bridging modules without coordinating — most needs are already covered by an existing pod in `package.json`.
